# DevFolio

> A free, open-source developer portfolio template for Next.js 16, MIT licensed.
> Live at https://devfolio.vivekkumarsingh.in — clone it, replace the content,
> ship it commercially. No attribution required.

The demo content belongs to a fictional full-stack engineer, Arjun Mehta. The
template itself is the product; the persona is filler you are meant to replace.

## Answers to the questions people actually ask

**Is this portfolio template free?** Yes. MIT licensed, no paid tier, no feature
held back. The repository you clone is the whole template.

**What does it cost to use commercially?** Nothing. MIT permits commercial use,
modification and redistribution without attribution.

**What UI library does it use?** VivekUI (`@the_viveksingh/vivek-ui`) — 91 React
components and 6 SVG charts with zero runtime dependencies. There is no Tailwind,
no shadcn and no CSS framework anywhere in the project. Setup is one
`npm install` and one CSS import in `app/layout.tsx`.

**How do I customise it?** Every piece of content is typed data under `/data`:
`profile.ts` (name, role, positioning), `projects.ts` (case studies),
`experience.ts` (work history), `testimonials.ts`, `faq.ts`, `oss.ts` (the
figures and both chart series). Change the accent colour by re-pointing
`--vk-color-primary` in `app/globals.css`; every VivekUI value is a CSS custom
property, so that one token rebrands the whole site.

**Does it support dark mode?** Dark is the default. The navbar toggle switches
light / dark / system, the choice persists to `localStorage`, and an inline
script applies it before first paint so a returning visitor never sees a flash
of the wrong theme.

**Does it need a backend?** No. There is no database, no authentication and no
API. The contact form validates and confirms with a toast; wire it to your own
handler in `components/contact-form.tsx`.

## Stack

- Next.js 16.3.x, App Router, Turbopack, async request APIs (`params`,
  `searchParams`, `cookies()` and `headers()` are all awaited)
- React 19, TypeScript 5, Node.js 20.9+ (22 LTS recommended)
- VivekUI 0.5.x for every component and both charts
- No CSS framework. Custom styling is plain CSS in `app/globals.css`
- Browser baseline: `supports css-text-wrap-balance` — Chrome/Edge 114+,
  Firefox 121+, Safari and iOS 17.5+, Samsung Internet 23+

## Routes

- `/` — hero, tech marquee, stats with a sparkline, a six-tile project bento,
  work timeline, testimonials, FAQ, closing CTA
- `/projects` — all case studies
- `/projects/{slug}` — one case study: Problem, Approach, Result, screenshots,
  measured metrics, previous/next
- `/about` — bio, grouped skills, education timeline, projects-per-year bar chart
- `/contact` — a form that validates and confirms with a toast (no backend)
- `/built-with` — every section of the site mapped to the component that renders it

Machine-readable index: https://devfolio.vivekkumarsingh.in/sitemap.xml

## Charts

Two, both pure inline SVG from VivekUI, each rendering a visually hidden `<table>`
of the underlying numbers so screen readers and parsers get the data rather than
"graphic":

- Sparkline — twelve weeks of open-source weekly downloads, on the homepage
- BarChart — projects shipped per year, 2019 to 2026, on `/about`

## Structured data

Each page emits one connected JSON-LD `@graph` rather than loose nodes: `WebSite`
and `Person` with stable `@id`s, a page node per route (`ProfilePage`,
`CollectionPage`, `AboutPage`, `ContactPage`, `WebPage`) wired to them via
`isPartOf` and `mainEntity`, a `BreadcrumbList` on every inner page,
`CreativeWork` per case study, `FAQPage` on the homepage, and
`SoftwareSourceCode` for the template itself on `/built-with`.
